items.titleEn: Gold price testing support near $3,600 as US Consumer Confidence sees sharp rise in November
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold prices have dropped to session lows as improving consumer confidence reduces demand for the safe-haven asset. The Consumer Confidence Index jumped to 103.3 in November, up from 91.9 in October, the Conference Board announced Tuesday. The data significantly exceeded economists’ expectations for a reading of around 92.4. “Consumer confidence rallied again in November, potentially due to lower uncertainty following the midterm elections,” said Fergus McCormick, Senior Economist, Global Indicators, at the Conference Board. “After two months of consecutive increases, the headline index is back to levels of confidence last seen in January 2025.”

items.titleEn: Why SpaceX shares are falling on Tuesday?
items.summaryEn: Buy SpaceX (SPCX). The stock is down on AI legal noise and compute-competition worries, but analysts still see durable vertical integration: dominant launch + Starlink cash flows funding AI infrastructure. Even if Grok Imagine faces setbacks, SpaceX’s AI division is already a major revenue contributor and the company can pivot compute leasing while Starlink demand supports the core business. The market is over-discounting near-term headlines versus long-run infrastructure positioning. Key Risk: Courts or regulators force a material shutdown or permanent limits on Grok/X AI features, cutting AI revenue faster than SpaceX can replace it with compute leasing. Sell/short Anthropic-linked exposure (use an AI infrastructure proxy like NVDA puts or a basket short of AI model developers) because the news highlights that SpaceX’s AI revenue can be terminated with 90 days’ notice and that lenders worry about chip deployment. If SpaceX can’t sustain competitive model development, compute-leasing demand could churn, pressuring pricing power across the AI stack.

items.titleEn: Insmed stock surges 14% on Sanofi's $41B acquisition; analysts see strategic fit
items.summaryEn: Buy Insmed (INSM) for the $175 cash deal. The stock already jumped on the announcement, but the spread to the offer price can still pay if deal momentum holds and financing/approvals stay on track. The rationale is simple: Sanofi is paying a big premium and has committed financing; the market will keep repricing toward deal certainty until closing in H1 2027. Key Risk: Deal breaks or gets delayed materially (regulatory/antitrust or financing/terms), widening the spread and forcing INSM down from the offer price. Buy Sanofi (SNY) for a sustained rerating tied to respiratory diversification. The acquisition adds Brinsupri and Arikayce plus late-stage pipeline, directly cushioning the 2031–32 Dupixent patent cliff and improving growth visibility. The thesis is that investors will pay up for a clearer post-2032 revenue path, not just a one-time premium.

items.titleEn: Why Intel stock is sliding on Tuesday?
items.summaryEn: Nvidia surged 31.5% Monday, then fell ~5% premarket Tuesday as AI profit-taking hit the whole group. That’s a classic overreaction setup: the news flow is still AI-led, and the selloff is broad-market/positioning rather than a fundamental break. Buy NVDA on weakness to capture the next leg of AI demand sentiment. Key Risk: A real demand slowdown shows up (cloud/AI capex guidance cut) rather than just profit-taking. Intel is sliding on a mix of fundamentals and guidance: foundry losses ($1.85B operating loss in Q3), Q4 revenue guide ($15–16B) below expectations (~$17B), and component shortages that could last into 2027. The stock’s Monday pop was tied to an 18A-P external customer win, but the customer wasn’t named and the business is still loss-making. Sell INTC now while the market is de-risking semis after Nvidia’s sharp rebound faded.

items.titleEn: Meta stock falls as Class C share delay raises questions over AI funding
items.summaryEn: Buy Meta Platforms (META). The Class C issuance is delayed, but the core AI build (chips, data centers, Muse/Enterprise) continues; the market is over-penalizing a timing issue. JPMorgan flags valuation back near pre-Muse levels while still expecting solid fundamentals, and the stock already priced in much of the “spending concern” narrative. If the lawsuit drags, the at-the-market sale just shifts later—not the AI roadmap. Key Risk: The Delaware case ultimately blocks the Class C structure or forces a worse-than-expected capital plan, forcing Meta to cut AI spending or dilute economics. Buy 3–6 month out-of-the-money put options on META. The news creates headline-driven volatility around the April 19, 2027 trial timeline and any interim court rulings. This protects against a renewed selloff if investors reprice the probability of a funding disruption while you hold the META long.

items.titleEn: Gold struggles to extend rebound as Fed rate hike bets pressure silver - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold prices were modestly lower and silver prices were sharply lower in early U.S. trading Tuesday, as a firm U.S. dollar and expectations for additional Federal Reserve interest rate increases continued to pressure precious metals ahead of key inflation figures. Gold struggled to extend Monday's recovery from a 14-month low, while silver gave back part of its recent rebound amid concerns about industrial demand and restrictive monetary policy. Renewed tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz provided limited support to bullion as investors remained focused on the outlook for interest rates. At approximately 8:37 a.m. EST, spot gold was trading near $3,621.70 an ounce, down $12.50, or 0.34%, while silver was trading near $42.040 an ounce, down $1.000, or 2.33%, on the session. Gold had traded between $3,606.80 and $3,679.00 during the day, while silver's range extended from $41.710 to $44.080. Monday's U.S. economic data indicated that business activity continued expanding in November, although growth moderated as elevated prices and tighter financial conditions constrained demand. The preliminary S&P Global U.S. composite purchasing managers' index declined to 54.6 from 55.9 in October, its lowest reading since July. The manufacturing PMI eased to 54.5 from 54.9, while the services PMI declined to 54.7 from 56.1, falling below expectations for a reading near 55.5. New orders continued increasing but at their slowest pace in four months, while employment growth remained relatively firm as companies worked to reduce outstanding orders. Input costs and selling price increases moderated but remained elevated, reinforcing concerns that inflation could persist above the Federal Reserve's target. The figures followed Friday's University of Michigan consumer sentiment report, which indicated that one-year inflation expectations declined to 3.7% from 4.7% in October , while longer-term expectations eased to 3.3% from 3.5%. The combination of slowing business activity and persistent price pressure continued to complicate the outlook for monetary policy.

items.titleEn: Dell stock on edge ahead of earnings as HP Enterprise guidance disappoints
items.summaryEn: Buy HPE. The article shows orders +72% and operating profit +110%, plus pricing power (up to 45% months after contracts) in networking and servers. If Dell’s earnings wobble, investors may rotate to the clearer execution story—HPE is already demonstrating it can monetize demand. Key Risk: HPE’s next-quarter guidance also disappoints or pricing power fades, showing the current AI/server demand surge is temporary. Sell DELL. HPE’s guidance disappointed versus expectations, and Dell is a close read-through for hyperscaler/server demand. With Dell already in a downward trend and options pricing implying a violent move, the skew favors downside if guidance/margins wobble. Target: $300 if the market de-risks AI server spending.

items.titleEn: Anthropic shares drop below $83 IPO price in premarket trading: here's why
items.summaryEn: Buy ANT. The stock is being sold for valuation/infrastructure fears, but the news adds a different catalyst: credible “slow/hold back” safety posture. That reduces tail-risk of a major regulatory or product-backlash event and supports enterprise adoption of Claude as a safer, more governable model provider. Also, MSCI index inclusion from Nov 30 can create mechanical demand from passive funds, tightening float after the IPO selloff. Key Risk: A sharp deterioration in AI demand or a broader AI de-rating that overwhelms any index/quality support and keeps ANT stuck below IPO-level multiples. Sell ARKQ (ARK Genomic Revolution ETF) or short a high-beta AI basket exposure like QQQ on rallies. The article shows the pattern: record AI debuts (ANT, SpaceX) quickly reverse as investors reprice stretched valuations and rising capex. Use this to fade “IPO hype” momentum while the market digests infrastructure cost pressure and safety headlines that can delay releases.

items.titleEn: SpaceX, Tesla push for year-end merger as five directors take charge of talks: report
items.summaryEn: Buy TSLA. The news signals serious, structured merger work (special committees + major banks + target timeline). That usually compresses downside because a deal path reduces the probability of a standalone “bad outcome,” and it creates a bid for Tesla equity ahead of any exchange-ratio talks. Expect volatility, but the direction is up if negotiations progress. Key Risk: Deal breaks or exchange ratio turns clearly unfavorable to Tesla shareholders. Sell any SpaceX-linked private exposure you hold (e.g., secondary shares/notes tied to SpaceX equity). The article highlights governance friction and regulatory risk (US defense/national security) plus Musk-related scrutiny. Even if talks continue, SpaceX’s control structure (Musk’s super-votes) and potential regulatory delays make SpaceX-side equity a worse risk/reward than Tesla-side.

items.titleEn: Why is Nvidia stock plunging 5% just a day after its historic comeback?
items.summaryEn: Buy NASDAQ:NVDA. The selloff is driven by politics and export-control noise, but Nvidia’s fundamentals are intact: revenue growth is still explosive and the next-quarter outlook remains huge. The blacklist is about access/controls through distributors, not a proven violation, and Nvidia already assumes no China data-center compute in its forecast—so incremental damage is likely limited versus the market’s 5% giveback. Expect dip-buying once the Senate hearing date is digested and compliance steps (new committee/C-suite) reduce perceived governance risk. Key Risk: A real export-control finding or new rule that directly blocks Nvidia’s ability to sell restricted AI chips into China (not just distributor complications). Sell short SOXX? No—use a cleaner proxy: short NASDAQ:AVGO (Broadcom). It has meaningful AI/infra exposure and is more sensitive to tightening cross-border chip flows and distributor restrictions. If Washington scrutiny expands beyond Nvidia’s specific channels, the market will reprice the whole “AI buildout” supply chain tied to China demand, even if end demand stays strong. This is a momentum/positioning trade against second-round risk: investors rotate away from China-exposed AI infrastructure names after each new blacklist.
